{{Short description|Vector space with a binary relation}}
In mathematics, specifically in [[order theory]], a [[binary relation]] <math>\,\leq\,</math> on a [[vector space]] <math>X</math> over the [[Real number|real]] or [[complex number]]s is called '''Archimedean''' if for all <math>x \in X,</math> whenever there exists some <math>y \in X</math> such that <math>n x \leq y</math> for all positive integers <math>n,</math> then necessarily <math>x \leq 0.</math> 
An '''Archimedean (pre)ordered vector space''' is a (pre)[[ordered vector space]] whose order is Archimedean.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=204–214}} 
A pre[[ordered vector space]] <math>X</math> is called '''almost Archimedean''' if for all <math>x \in X,</math> whenever there exists a <math>y \in X</math> such that <math>-n^{-1} y \leq x \leq n^{-1} y</math> for all positive integers <math>n,</math> then <math>x = 0.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|p=254}}

== Characterizations ==

A pre[[ordered vector space]] <math>(X, \leq)</math> with an [[order unit]] <math>u</math> is Archimedean preordered if and only if <math>n x \leq u</math> for all non-negative integers <math>n</math> implies <math>x \leq 0.</math>{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=139-153}}

== Properties ==

Let <math>X</math> be an [[ordered vector space]] over the reals that is finite-dimensional. Then the order of <math>X</math> is Archimedean if and only if the positive cone of <math>X</math> is closed for the unique topology under which <math>X</math> is a Hausdorff TVS (topological vector space).{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=222–225}}

== Order unit norm ==

Suppose <math>(X, \leq)</math> is an ordered vector space over the reals with an [[order unit]] <math>u</math> whose order is Archimedean and let <math>U = [-u, u].</math> 
Then the [[Minkowski functional]] <math>p_U</math> of <math>U</math> (defined by <math>p_{U}(x) := \inf\left\{ r > 0 : x \in r [-u, u] \right\}</math>) is a norm called the '''order unit norm'''. 
It satisfies <math>p_U(u) = 1</math> and the closed unit ball determined by <math>p_U</math> is equal to <math>[-u, u]</math> (that is, <math>[-u, u] = \{ x\in X : p_U(x) \leq 1 \}.</math>{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=139-153}}

=== Examples ===

The space <math>l_{\infin}(S, \R)</math> of bounded real-valued maps on a set <math>S</math> with the pointwise order is Archimedean ordered with an order unit <math>u := 1</math> (that is, the function that is identically <math>1</math> on <math>S</math>). 
The order unit norm on  <math>l_{\infin}(S, \R)</math> is identical to the usual sup norm: <math>\|f\| := \sup_{} |f(S)|.</math>{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=139-153}}

== Examples ==

Every [[order complete]] [[vector lattice]] is Archimedean ordered.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=250–257}} 
A finite-dimensional vector lattice of dimension <math>n</math> is Archimedean ordered if and only if it is isomorphic to <math>\R^n</math> with its canonical order.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=250–257}} 
However, a totally ordered vector order of dimension <math>\,> 1</math> can not be Archimedean ordered.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=250–257}} 
There exist ordered vector spaces that are almost Archimedean but not Archimedean.

The [[Euclidean space]] <math>\R^2</math> over the reals with the [[lexicographic order]] is {{em|not}} Archimedean ordered since <math>r(0, 1) \leq (1, 1)</math> for every <math>r > 0</math> but <math>(0, 1) \neq (0, 0).</math>{{sfn|Narici|Beckenstein|2011|pp=139-153}}
